title: Continuous batching cost scenarios and concurrency sizing (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This working draft lays out a spreadsheet-ready cost + sizing model for continuous batching + concurrency. The goal is to convert workload observations (QPS, request size distribution, p50/p95 response targets, KV-cache hit rates) into recommend concurrency targets, per-GPU batch sizing, and expected cost per 1M tokens. This is an iterative doc for the serving/runtime team — not final.

High-level assumptions (spreadsheet inputs):
- Workload QPS (requests/sec): input A. Typical study values: 10, 50, 200, 1000.
- Avg tokens per request: input B (tokens). Use median and 90th percentile columns.
- Model variant throughput baseline: tokens/sec per GPU at concurrency=1 and no batching/kv-cache: input C (measured).
- KV-cache effective hit rate: input D (0.0-1.0). When hit, cost of new tokens reduces dramatically (assume 5-10x cheaper).
- Continuous-batching window (ms): input E. Typical: 1, 5, 20, 50.
- Max batching size constraint (tokens per batch / sequences per batch): input F (set by memory/kv cache constraints).
- Target p95 latency SLO (ms): input G (e.g., 200 ms).
- Hardware profile: GPU type -> throughput curve (tokens/sec vs context length). Input H = GPU family multiplier.
- Queueing discipline: FIFO single queue per worker, head-of-line blocking allowed.

Core formulas (spreadsheet-friendly):
1) Effective tokens/sec per GPU (T_eff):
   T_eff = base_tokens_per_sec * batching_amplification * (1 - kv_hit_rate) + cached_tokens_per_sec * kv_hit_rate
   - base_tokens_per_sec = input C.
   - cached_tokens_per_sec = input C * cached_multiplier (default 4x since KV hits skip full decode).
   - batching_amplification approximates how many concurrent requests are packed into the GPU attention pass; modeled as:
       batching_amplification = min(1 + floor(Q * E / 1000), max_batch_multiplier)
     where Q = concurrency per worker, E = batching window ms. (Spreadsheet should use a smoother logistic approximation instead of floor for continuous cells.)

2) Latency model (per-request p95):
   p95_latency = service_latency + queue_wait_95
   - service_latency approximated from per-token decode time: tokens_per_request / (T_eff / concurrency) + batching_overhead_ms.
   - queue_wait_95 modeled by M/M/c approximation with c = number_of_workers * concurrency_per_worker. For rough engineering-level estimates we use Erlang C approximation (spreadsheet contains helper columns for traffic intensity rho = lambda / (c * mu)).

3) Cost per 1M tokens:
   cost_1M = (cost_per_gpu_hour * hours_to_generate_1M_tokens) / amortization_factor
   - hours_to_generate_1M_tokens = 1_000_000 / (T_eff * GPUs_allocated)
   - GPUs_allocated = ceil( (QPS * avg_tokens_per_request) / (T_eff) ) distributed across worker pool.

Key spreadsheet tabs and column definitions (for the linked sheet):
- Inputs: keys above (QPS, avg tokens, kv_hit, batching window, latency SLO, GPU type, spot/ondemand cost).
- Perf-profiles: measured base_tokens_per_sec per model / context length / GPU. Attached as measured CSV export.
- Scenarios: each row = scenario with inputs + computed T_eff, GPUs_needed, cost_1M, p95_latency_est.
- Sensitivity: vary kv_hit (0->0.9), batching_window (1->50ms), concurrency_per_worker (1->128) and compute percentiles.
- Recommended-config: map from scenario -> recommended concurrency_per_worker, batching_window, autoscale threshold.

Queueing & p95 tail guidance (engineering notes):
- Continuous batching reduces per-token compute by amortizing attention, but it increases variance in queue wait. Small windows (1-5ms) usually preserve low p95 at low QPS; larger windows (20-50ms) can cut cost 10-40% at the expense of increasing p95 tail.
- Use Erlang-C to estimate queue_wait_95 only for utilization < 0.95. Above 0.95 the model becomes unstable — flag as 'unsafe' in the sheet.
- For p95 safety add a headroom multiplier H = max(1.0, 1 + (utilization - 0.7)*2) applied to queue_wait_95 so the spreadsheet doesn't underpredict tails in bursty traffic.

KV-cache interaction (important, spreadsheet hooks):
- Two traffic classes: cache-hit and cache-miss. We model them as superposition:
   aggregate_T_eff = T_eff_miss * (1 - hit) + T_eff_hit * hit
   T_eff_hit uses reduced per-token cost and is less sensitive to batching window (hits often short-circuited).
- Recommendation: when hit_rate > 0.4, prefer smaller batching windows and higher concurrency_per_worker to reduce queueing; the cost per token already benefits from hits so scheduling should prioritize latency.

Example scenario table (illustrative numbers you can paste into the sheet):
- Scenario A: QPS=50, avg_tokens=80, kv_hit=0.2, batch_window=5ms, concurrency=8, GPU=A100(80GB)
   -> base_tokens_per_sec=1500, cached_multiplier=4x -> T_eff≈1500*(1+floor(8*5/1000))*(0.8)+6000*0.2 = approx 2400 tokens/sec per GPU
   -> GPUs_needed = ceil( (50*80) / 2400 ) = ceil(4000/2400)=2 GPUs
   -> p95_latency_est ≈ 110ms (service ~60ms + queue_wait_95 ~50ms)
   -> cost_1M ≈ using $3.2/hr -> hours = 1_000_000/(2400*2)=208 hrs -> cost ≈ $666 (note: remove amortization for reserved contracts)
- Scenario B: QPS=200, avg_tokens=120, kv_hit=0.05, batch_window=20ms, concurrency=32, GPU=H100
   -> shows large batching_amplification but high queueing; utilization ~0.9 -> p95 hairball -> recommend increasing workers rather than pushing concurrency further.

Operational recommendations (practical):
1) Add these derived columns to our per-model perf catalog so SRE / SE can run 'what-if' quickly.
2) Default starting point for new workloads: concurrency_per_worker = min(16, max(4, floor(target_p95_ms / 25))) and batch_window = 5ms with kv-aware adjustments.
3) Autoscale policy: scale up when 30s moving avg utilization > 0.65; scale down only when < 0.35 for 3m. This reduces oscillation and keeps p95 stable.
4) Canary safety checks: before flip to higher concurrency or larger window run traffic-replay for 10 minutes and assert p95 delta < +15% and error rate slope unchanged.

Instrumentation & experiments to run (spreadsheet rows linked to experiments):
- A) Vary batch_window with fixed QPS at 100 to map latency tail vs cost. Collect p50/p95/p99, token throughput, GPU util, queue depth histogram. (owner: Priya)
- B) KV-hit ablation: synthetic workload that toggles cache hits to measure cached_multiplier. (owner: Diego)
- C) Concurrency sweep: concurrency=1,2,4,8,16,32 with autoscale off to measure batching_amplification curve. (owner: Samira)
- D) Erlang vs trace-based tail: validate Erlang-C estimates against observed trace histograms and tune headroom multiplier. (owner: Alex)

Open questions / risks:
- How to model variable request sizes more elegantly than mean tokens? Proposal: include distribution buckets (p10/p50/p90) and compute service_latency as mixture model in the sheet.
- Cold-start impact on p95 for private deployments with smaller per-customer pools: need separate per-customer scenario tab.
- Batch-friendly kernels vs short-context models: some models have nonlinear scaling; the linear batching_amplification is a simplification. We should add a per-model nonlinearity coefficient.

Next steps (concrete):
- Populate the linked Google Sheet with perf CSV exports and run scenarios from the Example scenario list (week of 2026-03-02).
- Run experiments A-D (owners above). Track in Jira CON-3421.
- After experiments, produce a final Recommendations one-pager for product & sales packaging (deadline 2026-04-15).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally terse; the sheet is where most of the math lives. Please add objections / alternative headroom multipliers inline or assign to me. If you want different defaults for enterprise customers with private pools, add a new Scenario tab with "private" tag.

Raw paste-friendly formulas for the sheet (Excel/Sheets expressions):
- rho = (QPS * avg_tokens / tokens_per_sec_per_gpu) / (GPUs_allocated)
- GPUs_allocated = CEILING((QPS * avg_tokens) / T_eff)
- batching_amp = 1 + LOG(1 + (concurrency * batch_window_ms)/10)  /* smooth approx */
- p95_queue_wait = IF(rho<0.95, ErlangC_wait_formula, "unsafe_util")

-- Alex
